provisions.title: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
provisions.text: The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

provisions.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
provisions.text: Every API endpoint that receives an ID of an object, and performs any action on the object, should implement object-level authorization checks. The checks should validate that the logged-in user has permissions to perform the requested action on the requested object.

provisions.title: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
provisions.text: The product generates a hash for a password, but it uses a scheme that does not provide a sufficient level of computational effort that would make password cracking attacks infeasible or expensive.

provisions.title: Broken Object Property Level Authorization
provisions.text: APIs tend to expose endpoints that return all object’s properties. This is particularly valid for REST APIs.

provisions.title: Warning or costs for false or frivolous complaint
provisions.text: (12) At any stage after receipt of a complaint, if the Board is of the opinion that the complaint is false or frivolous, it may issue a warning or impose costs on the complainant.

examples.label: positive
negative

value.reason: server.ts:430 protects /rest/user/authentication-details only with security.isAuthorized(), which checks that the caller is logged in. server.ts:640 sends that route to authenticatedUsers(), and routes/authenticatedUsers.ts:12 runs UserModel.findAll() with no where clause, no ownership filter and no role check. So any logged-in user can read every user's record. Per models/user.ts, those records include username, email, password hash, lastLoginIp, profileImage and other sensitive fields. This matches the positive example: an unscoped findAll behind a login-only check, returned to the caller. That breaks object-level and property-level authorization and fails the access-control safeguards required for personal data. The Evidence does not show the response handler, so how much is masked before sending is not visible here. Even so, the unscoped read of all users' profile data is confirmed by the query and the route wiring.
